extracted.intended_audience: content strategists, news editors, and digital publishers
extracted.subtask_description: A short industry-applied checklist of seven traditional news values to help editors and content strategists prioritize and choose stories (timeliness, proximity, impact, prominence, oddity, relevance, conflict).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: "An event is more newsworthy the sooner it is reported."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use timeliness to prioritize breaking or newly unfolding stories; events reported sooner are considered more newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Events are more newsworthy the closer they are to the community reading about them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give higher priority to events geographically or culturally close to the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: "Events are more newsworthy when they affect a greater number of people."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess stories by the scale of people affected—broader impact increases news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Events are more newsworthy when they involve public figures."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories involving well-known individuals or institutions typically carry higher news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oddity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Events are more newsworthy the more out of the ordinary they are."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual, surprising, or atypical events can increase interest and newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Events are more newsworthy when they involve an issue that is top of mind in the public."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories that connect to current public concerns or ongoing conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: "Events are more newsworthy when they involve disagreement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories featuring disagreement, controversy, or confrontation often attract attention and merit prioritization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial weighting and audience/mission tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful content doesn't require checking all seven boxes—different organizations may weight values differently based on audience and mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the seven values as a flexible framework rather than a strict checklist; adapt weights according to organizational goals and audience preferences.
